slices.name: ws16-01-the-record-the-switches-and-one-seam
slices.brief:
Opens WS16's record and builds the one seam every email goes through. Today mail leaves the site through two Resend calls that build two different bodies: sendEmail in functions/utils/email.ts (lines 55 to 79, the fetch at line 59) and sendViaResend in functions/utils/admin/campaigns.ts (lines 164 to 204, the fetch at line 171). This step moves both behind deliver() in a new folder, functions/utils/mail/, with the sending service chosen by a server constant, MAIL_SENDER, set to 'resend'; gathers today's sender addresses into one module, domain/mail/addresses.ts, the one place every address lives (decision 28); adds the newsletter's switch, mailLists, and its server half, MAIL_LISTS_ON, both off; and changes nothing that is sent: every request leaves byte for byte as today, which a test holds against the literal bodies today's code writes. Nothing a visitor or a member meets changes. About eighteen files, most of them small; the lead's scout composes the brief from this entry. Line numbers are as 16c188a has them (the WS08 branch at its tenth step). WS16 starts from main once checkpoint L has merged; L's fix round touches none of the mail files, so the numbers should hold, and the scout confirms them with git diff 16c188a main -- <file> before the builder starts.

1. functions/utils/mail/switches.ts (new). The server half of the mail switches, constants only. Header comment: what each constant governs, that each caller imports it from this file and reads it inside the function at each call (never copied into a variable of its own module, so a test can turn it on through a getter on the mocked module, as test/integration/public-answer-trim.test.ts lines 32 to 58 do), and "Nothing here reads a setting of the environment." (the file must not contain the word env on its own, process. or import.meta: the pair test's fourth check). Contents, in this order:
   - export type MailSender = 'resend' (widened to 'resend' | 'ses' in WS16 step 7).
   - A comment block that starts "/**\n * Set: " and says: the LCA newsletter list in Group email for the LCA admins, the president and the media manager, the unsubscribe link, the email preferences page, the footer and the one-click headers on every optional email, and the mail engine's rules (the do-not-send list on every send path, no second try of a message that may have gone, the batch sizes of WORKERS_PLAN); "Turned on with mailLists in src/lib/features.ts, in the same change;" and "test/unit/mail-switches.test.ts holds the two equal."; then exactly one line: export const MAIL_LISTS_ON = false
   - A comment block on MAIL_SENDER: which service sends every email, 'resend' today; it changes only in a pull request of its own (the cutover, and the fallback is the same line back), never by a setting, so one deploy and one service send each message; then exactly one line: export const MAIL_SENDER: MailSender = 'resend'
2. functions/utils/mail/rules.ts (new). What the constants mean together, read at each call through ./switches: export function senderNow(): MailSender (MAIL_SENDER); export function engineRulesOn(): boolean (MAIL_LISTS_ON || MAIL_SENDER === 'ses'; written now so that WS16 step 7 widens the type and nothing else: with the type 'resend' alone, the comparison is written as a string comparison that typechecks, for example (MAIL_SENDER as string) === 'ses'). No other logic.
3. functions/utils/mail/send.ts (new). The seam.
   export type MailShape = 'single' | 'campaign' (the two request shapes Resend has been sent, kept apart so the move is byte for byte; WS16 step 12 drops the distinction with Resend).
   export interface OutgoingMail { from: string (the bare address); fromName?: string (the display name, SENDER_NAME when it is not given, so a club's mail can later carry the club's own name with no change to the seam, decision 6); to: string; replyTo: string; subject: string; html: string; text?: string; shape: MailShape }
   export interface MailEnv { RESEND_API_KEY: string }
   export type SendResult = { ok: true; providerId?: string } | { ok: false; status?: number; code?: string; noAnswer?: true; error: string }
   SENDER_NAME, today's display name in both bodies ('Louisiana Chess Association'), read from domain/mail/addresses.ts (item 18) and re-exported here for the transports
   export async function deliver(env: MailEnv, mail: OutgoingMail): Promise<SendResult>: reads senderNow() at each call and hands the message to the one transport it names (only sendThroughResend exists in this step); a fetch that throws is caught and answered { ok: false, noAnswer: true, error: <the thrown Error's message, or 'Unknown send error' for anything else> }. There is no fallback from one service to another inside a send: a message goes to exactly one service, so no message can be sent by both.
4. functions/utils/mail/resend.ts (new). export async function sendThroughResend(env: MailEnv, mail: OutgoingMail): Promise<SendResult>. POST https://api.resend.com/emails. For shape 'single' it writes exactly what functions/utils/email.ts lines 59 to 73 write today: headers { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${env.RESEND_API_KEY}` } and the body JSON.stringify({ from: `${mail.fromName ?? SENDER_NAME} <${mail.from}>`, to: [mail.to], reply_to: [mail.replyTo], subject, html, ...(mail.text ? { text: mail.text } : {}) }). For shape 'campaign' it writes exactly what functions/utils/admin/campaigns.ts lines 171 to 186 write: headers { Authorization: `Bearer ...`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } and JSON.stringify({ from: `${mail.fromName ?? SENDER_NAME} <${mail.from}>`, reply_to: [mail.replyTo], to: mail.to, subject, html }) (to as a bare string, reply_to first, no text). On a 2xx it answers { ok: true } without reading the body, as today; otherwise { ok: false, status: res.status, error: await res.text() }. This file and, from WS16 step 7, ses.ts are the only files under functions/ that name a mail service's address.
5. functions/utils/mail/outcome.ts (new). export type OutcomeKind = 'sent' | 'later' | 'never'; export function classifyToday(result: SendResult): OutcomeKind: 'sent' when ok; 'later' when noAnswer, or status 429 or 500 and above; 'never' otherwise: today's rule, moved word for word from functions/utils/admin/campaigns.ts lines 189 to 202. (WS16 step 2 adds classifyOnce and classify beside it.)
6. functions/utils/email.ts. sendEmail (lines 55 to 79) keeps its from and reply-to choice (lines 56 and 57) and becomes: const result = await deliver(env, { from, to: message.to, replyTo, subject: message.subject, html: message.html, text: message.text, shape: 'single' }); on a failure with noAnswer it throws new Error(result.error) (the same message a thrown fetch carries today); on any other failure it throws new Error(`Email send failed (${result.status}): ${result.error}`), today's words (line 77). EmailEnv (lines 37 to 41) is unchanged. DEFAULT_FROM and DEFAULT_REPLY_TO (lines 43 to 48, with their comments) move to domain/mail/addresses.ts (item 18), and email.ts re-exports both under the same names, so functions/utils/admin/campaigns.ts's import of them (line 2) and every other reader stay as they are. The doc comment at lines 50 to 54 is rewritten to say the transport is the seam (it holds no dash today, and the new words add none). trySendEmail (lines 86 to 94) is unchanged.
7. functions/utils/admin/campaigns.ts. sendViaResend (lines 164 to 204) becomes sendOne(env, to, subject, html): SendOutcome, calling deliver(env, { from: env.FROM_EMAIL ?? DEFAULT_FROM, to, replyTo: env.REPLY_TO_EMAIL ?? DEFAULT_REPLY_TO, subject, html, shape: 'campaign' }) and mapping the answer onto today's SendOutcome (lines 157 to 162): ok gives { ok: true }; noAnswer gives { ok: false, retryable: true, error: result.error }; any other failure gives { ok: false, retryable: classifyToday(result) === 'later', error: `Resend ${result.status}: ${result.error}` }, today's words (line 189), which the recipients' error column and the history show. sendTestEmail (line 217) and processCampaign (line 305) call sendOne. Nothing else in the file changes; the comments that named Resend's behaviour keep their meaning.

slices.name: ws16-02-migration-0060-and-the-do-not-send-gate
slices.brief:
Migration 0060 with the mail tables, the address rules, and the do-not-send gate on every send path. The tables are the final ones (decision 12, build once): lists, each marked whether it is one of LCA's main mailers (decision 18); the people a preference belongs to, keyed by address so that an address with no member account can hold one, with the person's own stop-all mark and a spam report's mark kept apart; the per-list choices; and the do-not-send list of dead addresses; plus four columns on the campaign tables the engine's rules need. Once the engine's rules are on (MAIL_LISTS_ON, or from WS16 step 7 MAIL_SENDER 'ses'), and for list mail whenever it is sent, the seam refuses, before any service is called, an address on the do-not-send list or under a reserved name (walk-in placeholders use .invalid), and for list mail an address that turned the list off, stopped all optional mail or, for a list that is not a main mailer, reported spam; event and account mail is never refused for a choice. The daily-emails worker's reminder phases, the registration-open notices and the director's announce each read their whole loop's addresses in one query and claim each row before its send, and under the rules the daily run sends its reminders before its rating lookups, so on the free plan its 50 outside calls go to mail first. Two settings join the switches: WORKERS_PLAN and the spam-report rule. Suites that hold today's path are pinned to it, so the switch-on change cannot turn them red. With the constant unset nothing reads the tables and every send is today's. About thirty files, nine of them figures a new migration moves; the lead's scout composes the brief from this entry. Line numbers are as 16c188a has them (the WS08 branch at its tenth step). WS16 starts from main once checkpoint L has merged; L's fix round touches none of the mail files, so the numbers should hold, and the scout confirms them with git diff 16c188a main -- <file> before the builder starts.

1. functions/db/schema.ts. Four tables, each with a one-line comment per column:
   - mailLists, 'mail_lists': id text primary key (a stable id: 'lca-newsletter' and 'lca-tournaments' now; a club list's id is chosen in part two); kind text not null ('newsletter', 'tournaments' or 'club'); name text not null (what a person reads: 'LCA newsletter'); mainMailer integer('main_mailer') not null default 0 (1 for LCA's main mailers, which a spam report made on other mail does not stop: decision 18); clubId text('club_id') references clubs.id with no action on delete (null for LCA's own lists; no cascade, because test/unit/migration-safety.test.ts follows only a dropped table's direct children (line 81), and a later rebuild of clubs must never cascade through a club's list into the choices people made on it); createdAt text('created_at') not null default (datetime('now')).
   - mailContacts, 'mail_contacts': id text primary key (32 hex characters, random; not a secret, since a link's signature is what cannot be guessed); address text not null (trimmed, lowercased), with a unique index mail_contacts_address_unique; optionalOffAt text('optional_off_at') (set only by the person's own choice, "Stop all optional email from LCA"); complainedAt text('complained_at') (set by a spam report while COMPLAINT_STOPS_OTHER_SENDERS holds; it stops the lists that are not main mailers and is never the person's own choice); createdAt.
   - mailListChoices, 'mail_list_choices': contactId text('contact_id') not null references mail_contacts.id on delete cascade; listId text('list_id') not null references mail_lists.id on delete cascade; choice text not null ('in' or 'out'); source text not null ('link', 'preferences', 'complaint', 'admin' or 'signup'); updatedAt text('updated_at') not null default (datetime('now')); primary key (contact_id, list_id); an index on (list_id, choice).
   - mailDoNotSend, 'mail_do_not_send': address text primary key (trimmed, lowercased); reason text not null ('bounce', or 'admin' for an address an LCA admin adds by hand in part two); detail text (the bounce's kind as Amazon names it, such as General, NoEmail, Suppressed or OnAccountSuppressionList, and nothing else of the notification); createdAt.
   - emailCampaigns gains listId text('list_id') (null for Group email's other audiences) and skippedCount integer('skipped_count') not null default 0 (recipients left out at send time because they turned the list off or their address stopped receiving mail after the send was made).
   - emailCampaignRecipients gains contactId text('contact_id') (the list recipient's contact, null for today's audiences) and sendingAt text('sending_at') (written just before the message is handed to the mail service; the engine's rules, WS16 step 4, never send a row with it set a second time).
   No CHECK constraint (the generator does not write them, and domain/mail/lists.ts names every value, held by a unit test); no REFERENCES on the four columns added to the campaign tables, so no table is rebuilt; today's CHECKs on the two status columns stay (migration 0021 line 15, 'sending', 'completed' or 'failed'; migration 0038 line 19, 'pending', 'sent' or 'failed'), so every state the engine writes is one of those values. 24 columns in all.

slices.name: ws16-03-the-links-the-footer-and-the-link-endpoints
slices.brief:
The server half of the member's side of every optional email: the signed links, the footer and the one-click headers, and the three public endpoints a link opens (the two pages that open them come in WS16 step 5). A link is signed with a key of its own, MAIL_LINK_SECRET, never expires, needs no sign-in and cannot be guessed; the header's link takes the one-click POST that RFC 8058 describes, and opening any link changes nothing until the person presses the page's one button. List mail always carries its headers and goes out through Amazon SES only (question 2). With MAIL_LISTS_ON unset the endpoints answer 404, unless a list email has already gone, in which case the links keep working whatever the constant says, since a sent unsubscribe link must keep working for at least 30 days (the FTC's CAN-SPAM guide). About twenty-three files, several of them one-line changes; the lead's scout composes the brief from this entry. Line numbers are as 16c188a has them (the WS08 branch at its tenth step). WS16 starts from main once checkpoint L has merged; L's fix round touches none of the mail files, so the numbers should hold, and the scout confirms them with git diff 16c188a main -- <file> before the builder starts.

1. functions/utils/mail/links.ts (new, pure Web Crypto, no import beyond domain/mail). export type LinkPurpose = 'unsubscribe' | 'preferences'. export async function signLink(secret: string, contactId: string, purpose: LinkPurpose, listId?: string): Promise<string>, the token `${contactId}.${scope}.${mac}`, where scope is the list id for an unsubscribe link and 'p' for a preferences link, and mac is the first 22 characters of the base64url HMAC-SHA256 of `lca-mail-link:1:${purpose}:${contactId}:${scope}` under the secret (132 bits: not guessable, and a token is about 70 characters). export async function readLink(keys: { current?: string; previous?: string }, token: string, purpose: LinkPurpose): Promise<{ contactId: string; listId?: string } | null>: splits on '.', recomputes the mac under the current key and, when given, the previous key, and compares in constant time (a small helper in this file, not functions/utils/stripe.ts's, so the worker bundles nothing of Stripe). No expiry and no date in the token. A missing current key: signLink throws a MailLinkKeyMissing error (the engine, WS16 step 4, treats it as a key fault and sends nothing), and readLink answers null. export async function linkKeyCheck(secret: string): Promise<string>: the first 16 hex characters of the HMAC-SHA256 of 'lca-mail-link-check' under the secret, which a list campaign stores when it is made (WS16 step 4), so a deployment whose copy of the key differs (the worker's is typed apart from the site's) knows before it sends a link that would not open; it reveals nothing usable about a 32-byte random key.
2. domain/mail/footer.ts (new, pure; read by the server's footer and by Group email's preview in WS16 step 5, so both say the same words). The footer is built in this one place, so a line could be added later in one small change; it holds no postal address (decision 23: no address in any email, and no setting, slot or reminder for one). The words of each LCA list, chosen by the list's id: for 'lca-newsletter', the reason "You're getting the LCA newsletter because this address is on an LCA member's account." and the label 'Unsubscribe from the LCA newsletter'; for 'lca-tournaments' (used from WS16 step 11), "You're getting LCA tournament email because this address is on an LCA member's account." and 'Unsubscribe from LCA tournament email'; PREFERENCES_LABEL = 'Email preferences'; EVENT_MAIL_STILL_COMES = "You'll still get email about your membership, registrations, payments and support requests." (what keeps coming after a person stops all optional mail: event and account mail, Group email's notes about a person's own membership among it).
3. functions/utils/mail/footer.ts (new). export async function listMailParts(env: { SITE_URL?: string; MAIL_LINK_SECRET?: string }, args: { contactId: string; listId: string }): Promise<{ footerHtml: string; headers: Array<{ name: string; value: string }> }>. It signs the unsubscribe token and the preferences token and builds: the header URL `${siteUrl}/api/mail/unsubscribe/${unsubscribeToken}`, the footer's links `${siteUrl}/email/unsubscribe/${unsubscribeToken}` and `${siteUrl}/email/preferences/${preferencesToken}` (siteUrl from resolveSiteUrl in functions/utils/site.ts, the configured site and never the request's host); the headers, in this order: { name: 'List-Unsubscribe', value: `<${headerUrl}>` } (one HTTPS URI and no mailto, since LCA has no mailbox that reads unsubscribe mail) and { name: 'List-Unsubscribe-Post', value: 'List-Unsubscribe=One-Click' }; the footer's HTML: the list's reason line, then the two links on one line joined by a middle dot as the layout's last line is, in the layout's ink colour at 13 and 12 pixels, links underlined in navy (contrast at least 4.5 to 1 on the footer's background).
4. functions/utils/emailLayout.ts. EmailLayout (lines 10 to 25) gains listFooter?: string (already-safe HTML); renderEmail (lines 130 to 194) draws it inside the footer cell above the "Louisiana Chess Association" line only when it is given. Without it the output is byte for byte today's for every template, which a test holds.
5. functions/utils/mail/send.ts. OutgoingMail gains headers?: Array<{ name: string; value: string }>. A message of kind 'optional', whenever it is sent and whatever the constants say: (a) with no listId, or with headers that are not List-Unsubscribe followed by List-Unsubscribe-Post with the one-click value, is refused with { ok: false, refused: 'not_list_mail', error: 'Not sent: an optional email must carry its unsubscribe headers.' } before any service is called (Refusal gains 'not_list_mail'), so no optional email can leave without them; (b) is never handed to Resend: while senderNow() is 'resend' it answers { ok: false, waitForSes: true, error: 'Not sent yet: list mail goes out through Amazon SES only.' }, which classifyOnce counts as later, so a newsletter caught by a move back to Resend waits, untried, until Amazon SES sends again (question 2: Resend's terms ask bulk mail to carry a postal address, which decision 23 leaves out, and to go only to people who opted in, and Resend suppresses an address that reports spam for every email of the account, receipts included). A test send (kind 'test') may go through either service, so the links can be tried before the cutover; through Resend it goes from DEFAULT_FROM (noreply@louisianachess.org, domain/mail/addresses.ts), the one address Resend is set up for (Resend sets up each subdomain on its own). The Resend transport's campaign shape adds headers: { 'List-Unsubscribe': ..., 'List-Unsubscribe-Post': ... } to its body only when the message carries headers (a test send's), so event mail's bytes are unchanged.
6. functions/utils/mail/rules.ts. export async function listLinksLive(db: D1Database): Promise<boolean>: true when MAIL_LISTS_ON, or when a list email is on record (SELECT 1 FROM email_campaigns WHERE list_id IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1), so a rollback of the switch can never break a link in mail already sent.
7. domain/contracts/mail.ts (new): unsubscribeResponseSchema, z.strictObject({ unsubscribed: z.literal(true), list: z.string(), preferencesToken: z.string() }) (the page links on to the preferences page with it); unsubscribeLinkResponseSchema, z.strictObject({ list: z.string() }) (the GET that asks for JSON); emailChoicesResponseSchema, z.strictObject({ address: z.string() (masked), lists: z.array(z.strictObject({ id: z.string(), name: z.string(), on: z.boolean() })), optionalOff: z.boolean() }); emailChoicesRequestSchema, z.object({ lists: z.record(z.string(), z.boolean()).optional(), optionalOff: z.boolean().optional() }). domain/contracts/index.ts exports them; domain/contracts/registry.ts gains 'mail/unsubscribe/[token]': { GET, POST } and 'mail/preferences/[token]': { GET, PATCH }. The ratchet: 17 contracted methods to 21, 127 api methods to 131, PENDING_COUNT 110 unchanged (test/unit/contracts-status.test.ts stays green and the K1d row is not touched).
8. functions/api/mail/unsubscribe/[token].ts (new). onRequestOptions (handleOptions), onRequestGet and onRequestPost. Every answer is 404 { error: "This link isn't working." } unless listLinksLive(env.DB) and readLink(...) verifies with purpose 'unsubscribe' and the contact and list exist. GET writes nothing: a request whose Accept header holds application/json (the page's own check, WS16 step 5) answers 200 { list: <the list's name> } with Cache-Control no-store; any other GET, which is what a mail program sends when it opens the header's address in a browser (RFC 8058 section 3.2 has the GET and the POST share the address, and Gmail opens it when it does not offer its own button), answers 303 to `${siteUrl}/email/unsubscribe/<token>` with Cache-Control no-store, so the person lands on the page with the button. POST writes the choice in one statement: INSERT INTO mail_list_choices (contact_id, list_id, choice, source) VALUES (?, ?, 'out', 'link') ON CONFLICT (contact_id, list_id) DO UPDATE SET choice = 'out', source = 'link', updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE choice <> 'out'; and it answers 200 { unsubscribed: true, list: <the list's name>, preferencesToken: <a fresh preferences token for the contact> } with Cache-Control no-store. It accepts any body, as RFC 8058 sections 3.1 and 3.2 have a mail provider send it: multipart/form-data or application/x-www-form-urlencoded carrying List-Unsubscribe=One-Click, and the page's own empty JSON; it reads no cookie and no sign-in, never answers a POST with a redirect (the RFC's rule is about the POST), and a second POST answers the same 200 and changes nothing. The list and the person come from the token alone.
9. functions/api/mail/preferences/[token].ts (new). onRequestOptions, onRequestGet, onRequestPatch; the same 404 rule with purpose 'preferences'. GET answers { address: maskAddress(contact.address), lists, optionalOff: contact.optional_off_at !== null }, where lists holds the newsletter only when the address is in its audience (an address on an account with an active membership: K's rule, decision 28, written once in functions/utils/mail/lists.ts, new here, which WS16 step 4's send reads too), whatever choice the contact holds on it, and any other list the contact holds a choice on (none in part one until WS16 step 11). A list's on is false when its choice is 'out', or, for a list that is not one of LCA's main mailers, while a spam report's mark stops it (complained_at set while COMPLAINT_STOPS_OTHER_SENDERS holds, and no 'in' choice on that list newer than the mark: the gate's rule, WS16 step 2). optionalOff is the person's own mark only. PATCH reads its body through parseBody(emailChoicesRequestSchema); a list key the GET would not show is 400 'That list is not one of yours.' and writes nothing, so an address outside the newsletter's audience, a lapsed member's among them, can never turn the newsletter on. On deletes the list's 'out' choice; for a list that is not a main mailer it also writes 'in' with source 'preferences' when the contact's complained_at is set, so the person's own newer choice lifts the report's mark for that list; it never writes 'in' on one of LCA's main mailers, whose audience alone decides who gets them (part two adds lists whose rule takes sign-ups, where on writes 'in'). Off writes 'out' with source 'preferences'; optionalOff true sets optional_off_at to now and false clears it, leaving the list choices as they are; it answers the GET's shape. Both answers carry Cache-Control no-store.

slices.name: ws16-04-the-newsletter-list-and-the-engine-rules
slices.brief:
The LCA newsletter list and the engine's rules, on the server. A newsletter is an ordinary campaign row with list_id set, so the claim, the sweep and the recipient rows are today's, and what is new is: who is on the list (every address on an account with an active membership, once: K's rule, decision 28, not widened unless K says so; less the people who turned it off or stopped all optional mail and the addresses that no longer receive mail, and never another address, whatever choice it holds); the per-recipient footer and one-click headers; a row that decides its own path (a list campaign is sent only by the list path, whatever MAIL_LISTS_ON says, so a revert of the switch-on change or a worker deploy that lags the site's cannot send the rest of a newsletter the old way); three rules under which no message can be sent twice (a row is marked just before its send and never sent again once marked, an answer that does not prove the message was refused is never tried again, and a throttle stops the run and puts the untried rows back); a check that the deployment sending a list campaign holds the link key it was made with; and batch sizes that stay inside the hosting plan's limits per run. The newsletter goes out only through Amazon SES (question 2): while Resend sends, its POST answers 409 and a list message waits. Four new admin methods, each with its contract, show, send, test and stop the newsletter, behind requireListMailer, a guard that verifies the session once; today's five campaign endpoints keep their files and their guard. With MAIL_LISTS_ON unset the new endpoints answer 404 and every line of today's campaign path runs as today. The newsletter's sends themselves are proved in WS16 step 7, where its only service, Amazon SES, arrives; this step proves who is on the list from the rows it writes, the engine's rules, the links and the test send. About seventeen files; the lead's scout composes the brief from this entry. Line numbers are as 16c188a has them (the WS08 branch at its tenth step). WS16 starts from main once checkpoint L has merged; L's fix round touches none of the mail files, so the numbers should hold, and the scout confirms them with git diff 16c188a main -- <file> before the builder starts.

1. domain/mail/addresses.ts (WS16 step 1) gains LIST_SENDERS: each LCA list's From address and display name, keyed by list id, the newsletter's now. Its values are the forms K decided once, together, from the lead's address map (decision 28), on Wednesday, November 11, 2026 (decision 37): the newsletter's entry holds newsletter@news.louisianachess.org with the display name "Louisiana Chess Association", and the module's comment marks it as decided by K on that date, never as pending. Replies go to the env's REPLY_TO_EMAIL or DEFAULT_REPLY_TO, as Group email's replies go today. No other file writes a sender address, so the switch-on change writes the decided forms in this one file.
2. functions/utils/mail/plan.ts (from WS16 step 2) gains the campaign sizes, with the arithmetic in comments: free: the request path sends one batch of 10 and stops, a sweep run sends 20 and touches one campaign; paid: the request path sends batches of 40 until a 20-second deadline, which it checks before each send, claiming no more rows than fit in the time left at SEND_INTERVAL_MS (functions/utils/admin/campaigns.ts line 155, 400 ms), so a batch never runs past waitUntil's 30 seconds; a sweep run sends up to 300 across up to 20 campaigns. A batch of n costs n outside calls and n + 8 database queries at most (the write-off, the campaign read, the claim, the gate, the first mark, n outcome batches each carrying the next mark, the count, the close), a run of the sweep 1 more; so on free Group email's request path for Specific people (today's POST, whose requireMailer verifies an LCA admin's session twice, functions/utils/auth.ts lines 194 to 205 and 222 to 230: two outside calls) costs at most 12 outside calls and 25 queries, and a sweep run at most 21 outside calls and 30 queries, against 50 and 50. The newsletter's own request path runs only on Workers Paid, since Amazon SES sends only there (question 3). export function sizes(): { requestBatch: number; requestDeadlineMs: number | null; sweepBatch: number; sweepCampaigns: number }, read from WORKERS_PLAN at each call.
3. functions/utils/mail/lists.ts (from WS16 step 3, which wrote the audience clause). The newsletter's audience, in one place: members whose membership_status is 'active' (K's rule, decision 28: "you need to be active to get the newsletter"; the list is not widened to lapsed members or to every account unless K says so), whose role is not 'guest', and whose email is not null or blank and is a list address (isListAddress's names written as clauses: no reserved top-level name and no example domain), each address trimmed and lowercased, once.

SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM email_campaigns WHERE list_id = ?list AND status = 'sending') (id `campaign-${Date.now().toString(36)}` as today, status 'sending', list_id, filter_json '{"list":"lca-newsletter","linkCheck":"<the 16 characters>"}'); INSERT OR IGNORE INTO mail_contacts (id, address) SELECT lower(hex(randomblob(16))), a.address FROM (the audience's distinct addresses) a; INSERT INTO email_campaign_recipients (id, campaign_id, member_id, email, contact_id) SELECT 'rcpt-' || ?campaign || '-' || c.id, ?campaign, NULL, c.address, c.id FROM mail_contacts c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM email_campaigns WHERE id = ?campaign) AND c.address IN (the audience) AND NOT EXISTS (an 'out' choice of c on the list) AND c.optional_off_at IS NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM mail_do_not_send d WHERE d.address = c.address) ORDER BY c.address; UPDATE email_campaigns SET total_recipients = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM email_campaign_recipients WHERE campaign_id = ?campaign) WHERE id = ?campaign. Every other campaign takes the rules under engineRulesOn() and today's path otherwise, where every line runs as today and test/integration/campaigns.test.ts passes unchanged:
   a. Before the claim, one batch writes off the campaign's rows left with sending_at set and a claim older than CLAIM_TIMEOUT (line 149): status 'failed', error "Not sent again: the mail service may have taken it, and a second try could send it twice.", and failed_count gains their number.
   b. claimRecipients (lines 247 to 269) also requires sending_at IS NULL and returns contact_id; a row already marked is never claimed again, by any run, on either service.
   c. processCampaign (lines 280 to 367) reads list_id and filter_json with subject and body_html. For a list campaign, before anything is claimed, the campaign's linkCheck is compared with linkKeyCheck (WS16 step 3) of this deployment's MAIL_LINK_SECRET, or of MAIL_LINK_SECRET_PREVIOUS while a key is being changed: a mismatch is a key fault, so nothing is claimed and the campaign's history says "Not sent yet: the link key on this deployment is not the one this email was made with."    d. Before each send the row's sending_at is written: the first row's in one UPDATE, and each later row's in the same batch that records the previous row's outcome, so a send still costs one query.
   e. For a list campaign each recipient's message is built by listMailParts (WS16 step 3) and renderEmail with its listFooter, and goes through the seam with kind 'optional', listId, the headers, from the list's entry in LIST_SENDERS (its From address and display name, domain/mail/addresses.ts) and reply-to as today; for today's audiences it is today's message, with kind 'event'.
   f. The outcome is classify(result) (WS16 step 2), and always classifyOnce for a list campaign: 'sent' as today; 'later' puts this row and every claimed row not yet tried back in the pool in one statement (claimed_at and sending_at NULL; attempts restored for the rows not tried, since claimRecipients counted them) and ends the run, so a throttle, a paused account, a key fault, a gate that could not be read or a list message held back from Resend never burns the batch; 'never' marks the row failed with the service's words, or for a request with no answer "No clear answer from the mail service; not sent again so it cannot arrive twice.". A missing key (MailLinkKeyMissing, or the service's key) is a key fault: the batch goes back untried and the first row's error says "Not sent yet: the mail key is missing on this deployment.".

slices.name: ws16-07-the-amazon-ses-sender
slices.brief:
The Amazon SES sender: a second transport behind the seam that signs its own requests with AWS Signature Version 4 inside the Worker runtime (Web Crypto only, no package), sends with SES's v2 SendEmail over HTTPS, and maps every answer onto the campaign sender's three kinds, sent, retry later and never, so that a message is tried again only when Amazon's answer proves it was not taken. MAIL_SENDER stays 'resend': the cutover is a pull request of its own after the switch-on change, once Amazon approves real sending, K's checks in the sandbox and the site's own test through Amazon SES pass and the account is on Workers Paid, and the way back is the same line back; one service sends each message, so none is sent by both. The newsletter goes out only through this sender (question 2). The cutover waits for Workers Paid (question 3): on the free plan's 10 ms of processor time an invocation, signing could cut a director's announcement to many entrants part way (announce.ts sends inside the request and writes its one activity row after the loop, lines 74 to 89), the request would end with error 1102, and the page, which keeps the message filled in on an error (src/pages/TournamentManagePage.tsx lines 1175 to 1199), would invite a second press that mails everyone already reached twice; Workers Paid gives 30 seconds. About twenty-six files; the lead's scout composes the brief from this entry. Line numbers are as 16c188a has them (the WS08 branch at its tenth step). WS16 starts from main once checkpoint L has merged; L's fix round touches none of the mail files, so the numbers should hold, and the scout confirms them with git diff 16c188a main -- <file> before the builder starts.

1. functions/utils/mail/sigv4.ts (new, pure Web Crypto). export async function signAwsRequest(args: { method: string; url: string; headers: Record<string, string>; body: string; region: string; service: string; accessKeyId: string; secretAccessKey: string; now: Date }): Promise<Record<string, string>>, returning the headers to send: the given ones, x-amz-date (the UTC time as 20261110T120000Z) and authorization. The canonical request (AWS's IAM guide, "Create a signed AWS API request"): the method; the path with each segment URI-encoded the AWS way (unreserved characters A to Z, a to z, 0 to 9, hyphen, period, underscore and tilde kept, every other byte as %XX in capitals); the query string (empty here, its line still written); the canonical headers, names lowercased and sorted, values trimmed, here content-type, host and x-amz-date, each line ending in a newline; the signed-headers list, content-type;host;x-amz-date; and the hex SHA-256 of the body. The string to sign: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256, the time, the scope `${date}/${region}/${service}/aws4_request`, and the hex SHA-256 of the canonical request, joined by newlines. The signing key: HMAC-SHA256 of the date under 'AWS4' + the secret, then of the region, the service and 'aws4_request' in turn, kept for the isolate's life in a Map keyed by access key id, date, region and service (never by the secret). The header: `AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Credential=${accessKeyId}/${scope}, SignedHeaders=${signed}, Signature=${hex}`.

Without both keys: { ok: false, keyMissing: true, error: 'No Amazon SES key on this deployment.' } and no request (so previews and tests without the keys send nothing; SendResult's failure gains keyMissing?, which configFault() counts). The body: { FromEmailAddress: `${mail.fromName ?? SENDER_NAME} <${mail.from}>`, Destination: { ToAddresses: [mail.to] }, ReplyToAddresses: [mail.replyTo], Content: { Simple: { Subject: { Data: mail.subject, Charset: 'UTF-8' }, Body: { Html: { Data: mail.html, Charset: 'UTF-8' }, ...(mail.text ? { Text: { Data: mail.text, Charset: 'UTF-8' } } : {}) }, ...(mail.headers ? { Headers: mail.headers.map((h) => ({ Name: h.name, Value: h.value })) } : {}) } }, ConfigurationSetName: SES_CONFIGURATION_SET, EmailTags: [{ Name: 'kind', Value: mail.kind }, ...(mail.listId ? [{ Name: 'list', Value: mail.listId }] : [])] }. POST https://email.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/v2/email/outbound-emails with content-type application/json, signed for the service 'ses'. A 200 answers { ok: true, providerId: <MessageId> }; any other status answers { ok: false, status, code, error: `Amazon SES ${status} ${code}: ${message}` }, with code read from the x-amzn-errortype header (before its first ':'), else from the body's __type or code (after its last '#'), and message from the body's message or Message; a fetch that throws answers { ok: false, noAnswer: true, error }.

The kinds (classifyOnce in functions/utils/mail/outcome.ts, written in WS16 step 2, holds this table; this step adds a unit case for each row): retry later, because Amazon's answer proves the message was not taken: 429 and TooManyRequestsException; ThrottlingException, which also carries "Maximum sending rate exceeded" and "Daily message quota exceeded"; 503 ServiceUnavailable; SendingPausedException and AccountSuspendedException (the run ends); and 401 or 403 with AccessDeniedException, UnrecognizedClientException, InvalidClientTokenId, SignatureDoesNotMatch, IncompleteSignature, ExpiredTokenException, MissingAuthenticationToken, NotAuthorized or OptInRequired, a key fault (the run ends and no attempt is counted); and NotFoundException and MailFromDomainNotVerifiedException, faults of the account's setup that every message of the run would meet (a configuration set misnamed, or made in another region, answers NotFoundException to every send), so the run ends with the rows back untried, as for a key fault. Never, and never tried again: MessageRejected, BadRequestException, ValidationError and ValidationException, LimitExceededException, 413 and every other 4xx; and 500 InternalFailure, 502, 504, 408 RequestTimeoutException and a request with no answer, because each may come after Amazon took the message, and trying again could send it twice. An address on Amazon's own suppression list is accepted with a MessageId and not delivered (the outside facts), so the site's own do-not-send list, read first, is what stops it.

slices.name: ws16-08-the-bounce-and-complaint-receiver
slices.brief:
The bounce and complaint receiver, and checkpoint M's close. Amazon publishes the configuration set's bounces and complaints to an SNS topic in K's account, and SNS posts each to one address on the site; the receiver acts on a notification only after it has proved, by its signature and its topic, that it came from that topic, is safe to receive twice, and stores only what the rules need: for a permanent bounce, the address, its kind and the time; for a spam report, the choice that stops the list it was pressed on and, by the setting, the mark that stops the person's mail from lists that are not LCA's main mailers (decision 18). Event and account mail, and LCA's main mailers other than the list pressed on, are never stopped by a spam report, and a report that says the message is not spam changes nothing. With the engine's rules off (MAIL_LISTS_ON unset and MAIL_SENDER 'resend') or with no topic bound, the endpoint answers 404 and fetches nothing. The step also writes checkpoint M's section, its pull request text, what reaches production, the switch-on change and the cutover change, each with its exact files, runs each one's gate on a throwaway branch before the merge, and gives K's list for them. About nineteen files; the lead's scout composes the brief from this entry. Line numbers are as 16c188a has them (the WS08 branch at its tenth step). WS16 starts from main once checkpoint L has merged; L's fix round touches none of the mail files, so the numbers should hold, and the scout confirms them with git diff 16c188a main -- <file> before the builder starts.

1. functions/utils/mail/sns.ts (new, pure Web Crypto). export interface SnsMessage { Type; MessageId; TopicArn; Message; Timestamp; SignatureVersion; Signature; SigningCertURL; Subject?; SubscribeURL?; Token?; UnsubscribeURL? }. export function stringToSign(m: SnsMessage): string | null: for Type 'Notification' the fields Message, MessageId, Subject (only when present), Timestamp, TopicArn, Type; for 'SubscriptionConfirmation' and 'UnsubscribeConfirmation' the fields Message, MessageId, SubscribeURL, Timestamp, Token, TopicArn, Type; each written as its name, a newline, its value and a newline (so the string ends with one newline), in that order, which is the byte order of the names; null for any other Type. export function certUrlAllowed(url: string, region: string): boolean: https, no port, no user or password, the host exactly `sns.${region}.amazonaws.com`, a path ending in .pem. export async function verifySnsMessage(m: SnsMessage, region: string, fetchCert: (url: string) => Promise<string>): Promise<'valid' | 'invalid' | 'cert_unreachable' | 'cert_unusable'>: SignatureVersion '1' (RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-1) or '2' (with SHA-256), anything else invalid; the cert URL allowed, else invalid; the PEM fetched (kept for the isolate's life in a Map keyed by URL; a failed fetch is cert_unreachable); its DER walked to the subjectPublicKeyInfo (Certificate, then tbsCertificate, then past the optional [0] version, the serial number, the signature algorithm, the issuer, the validity and the subject: about forty lines, no package) and imported as spki (a certificate fetched from the allowed host that cannot be walked or imported is cert_unusable); the base64 Signature verified over stringToSign. The trust rests on HTTPS to Amazon's SNS host for our region and on the topic check in the handler; the chain of the certificate is not walked (no certificate store in the Worker), which the record states.
2. functions/utils/mail/sesEvents.ts (new). export async function applySesEvent(db: D1Database, event: unknown, args: { accountId: string; complaintStopsOtherSenders: boolean }): Promise<{ bounces: number; complaints: number; ignored: boolean }>. The event's kind is eventType, or notificationType for an identity notification; event.mail.sendingAccountId must equal the account in our topic's ARN, else the event is ignored. Bounce with bounceType 'Permanent', unless its bounceSubType is EmailValidationSuppressed (a guess of Amazon's paid address validation, not a dead mailbox, which is skipped): for each bouncedRecipients[].emailAddress, normalized, INSERT OR IGNORE INTO mail_do_not_send (address, reason, detail) VALUES (?, 'bounce', <bounceSubType>), so a second copy of the same notification changes nothing. Bounce 'Transient' or 'Undetermined': nothing. Complaint, unless its complaintFeedbackType is 'not-spam' (a provider's word that the person rescued the message from the spam folder, which is skipped): for each complainedRecipients[].emailAddress, normalized: INSERT OR IGNORE the contact (an id from lower(hex(randomblob(16)))); when event.mail.tags.list[0] names a list in mail_lists, the 'out' choice on it with source 'complaint' (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET choice = 'out', source = 'complaint', updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE choice <> 'out'), so the list the report was pressed on stops at once, a main mailer included (decision 18); and, when complaintStopsOtherSenders, UPDATE mail_contacts SET complained_at = max(coalesce(complained_at, ''), datetime(?)), bound to the complaint's own timestamp (complaint.timestamp), so a new report moves the mark past an older 'in' choice and a retried copy of the same report changes nothing; the mark stops the lists that are not main mailers (none yet in part one) and is never the person's own stop-all, optional_off_at, which only the person sets. Every other kind (Delivery, Send, Reject, DeliveryDelay, Open, Click, Rendering Failure, Subscription): nothing. All of one event's writes in one db.batch. Nothing else of the notification is stored or logged: no diagnostic code, no headers, no feedback report, no network address, and the log line holds the counts, never an address.
3. functions/utils/mail/sns.ts also exports SNS_MAX_AGE_MS = 3 * 60 * 60 * 1000: a Notification whose Timestamp is older than three hours is answered 200 and changes nothing, so a stored copy of a signed bounce, replayed after an LCA admin clears the address (WS16 step 9), cannot put it back; SNS's own tries end within an hour under the delivery policy K sets on switch-on day (the checklist), well inside the window.
4. functions/api/mail/ses-events.ts (new). onRequestOptions and onRequestPost. 404 { error: 'Not found' } unless engineRulesOn() and env.SES_SNS_TOPIC_ARN is set (after the switch-on, MAIL_LISTS_ON makes it live while Resend still sends, so the subscription and the two simulator checks come before the cutover). Then, in this order, with nothing written and nothing fetched before the check that needs it: read the raw text (SNS sends text/plain by default) and JSON.parse it, 400 on failure; TopicArn must equal SES_SNS_TOPIC_ARN, else 400; the x-amz-sns-message-type header must equal Type, else 400; verifySnsMessage with SES_REGION: 400 when invalid (a signature that verifies false, a certificate URL that is not allowed, a version other than 1 or 2), 500 when the certificate cannot be fetched or, fetched from the allowed host, cannot be read (cert_unusable: after Amazon changes its certificate that is a fault of this code, and SNS tries again on a 5xx, where a 400 would be final and the notification lost); then by Type: SubscriptionConfirmation, its SubscribeURL must pass certUrlAllowed's host and https rules (without the .pem rule), else 400, and one GET of it confirms the subscription, 200; UnsubscribeConfirmation, 200 and one warning log line that names no address (it means the site's subscription was removed, which K's alarm list watches); Notification older than SNS_MAX_AGE_MS, 200 and nothing else; Notification, applySesEvent(JSON.parse(Message)) with the topic's account and COMPLAINT_STOPS_OTHER_SENDERS (WS16 step 2), 200 { received: true }; a database failure 500. Its contract: 'mail/ses-events': { POST: { response: z.strictObject({ received: z.literal(true) }) } } in domain/contracts/mail.ts and the registry (contracted 26 to 27 of 137); SNS's body is not checked by a request schema, as Stripe's webhook's is not.
5. functions/types.ts: Env gains SES_SNS_TOPIC_ARN?: string (a secret of the production Pages project only: it holds the account number, which stays out of the repository); vitest.integration.config.ts binds 'arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:000000000000:lca-mail-events'; test/a11y/global-setup.ts's A11Y_EMPTY_SECRETS gains it.
6. test/integration/harness.ts: a catch point for sns.us-east-1.amazonaws.com: a GET of a .pem path answers the test certificate the helper set (snsBehavior.certReachable false makes it 503); a GET whose query holds Action=ConfirmSubscription is recorded in snsConfirmations and answered 200. resetHarness resets both.
7. test/integration/helpers/sns.ts (new): makes an RSA key pair with crypto.subtle.generateKey, wraps its spki in a minimal X.509 certificate written by a small DER writer (version 3, a serial, sha256WithRSAEncryption, a one-name issuer and subject, a validity, the spki, an outer signature the receiver never checks), PEM-encodes it, and signs SNS messages of the three types with either version, so every case runs in the Workers runtime the site runs in.

verify_items.item: How SES reaches an HTTPS address
verify_items.finding: Confirmed by the outside facts: event destinations are CloudWatch, Firehose, EventBridge, Pinpoint and SNS, with no direct HTTPS one; SNS posts to an HTTPS subscription after a confirmation, each message signed (version 1 SHA-1, version 2 SHA-256) with a certificate at SigningCertURL, and AWS's guide says to check the certificate's host and reject an unexpected TopicArn; SNS tries again on 5xx and 429 (by default three more times, 20 seconds apart, then discards the message) and treats other answers as final; a delivery policy can stretch the tries to at most an hour, which K sets on switch-on day (the checklist), and an alarm on the topic's failed deliveries tells K when tries run out.

Not checked in AWS's words: the pages name the SHA1 and SHA256 hashes but not RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 outright, which is the standard reading. The integration test proves the code against keys it makes; the first real confirmation, on production after the switch-on, proves it against Amazon's, and a failure there answers 400 and leaves the subscription pending, which K sees in the SNS console before any mail depends on it.

Confirmed by the outside facts: SNS sends text/plain; charset=UTF-8 unless the topic sets otherwise, with the x-amz-sns-message-type, x-amz-sns-message-id and x-amz-sns-topic-arn headers; the handler reads the raw text.

Confirmed by the outside facts: complainedRecipients lists the addresses of the message's recipients on the reporting domain, which is the one address for the site's one-recipient sends; mail.tags carries the EmailTags given at send (kind and list); Gmail sends no complaint data to SES, so a spam report from a Gmail inbox never reaches the receiver.

verify_items.item: The Worker can verify RSA with SHA-1

verify_items.item: The two kinds a report can be that change nothing

sequencing_rationale:
The first part of WS16 gives the site its own mail engine and a first LCA newsletter, switched on in production in the week of Monday, November 16, 2026, from K's decisions of Tuesday, November 10, 2026: Amazon SES in place of Resend through one seam, with Resend as the fallback for event and account mail until SES has carried real mail cleanly for about 30 days; a bounce and complaint receiver and a do-not-send list; per-list opt-outs in the site's own tables with a one-click unsubscribe and a preferences page; and the LCA newsletter list, written in today's Group email text box and sent from that page by the LCA admins, the president and a new media manager. It goes right after WS08's checkpoint L, ahead of WS09 (decision 2). It is twelve steps on one branch, redesign/ws16-mail, cut from main once checkpoint L has merged, in three checkpoints lettered M, N and O: the record uses A to D for WS01, E to I for WS02 and J to L for WS08, and a letter names a pull request for good, so WS16 takes the next three. Each checkpoint is a draft pull request that merges on its own with production behaving exactly as today while its switch is off: checkpoint M's switch is mailLists with its server half MAIL_LISTS_ON, checkpoint N's is mailTools with MAIL_TOOLS_ON, and MAIL_SENDER stays 'resend' until the cutover's own change; checkpoint O, after the clean period, changes nothing a visitor meets because SES already sends everything. Every server change reads its constant at the request; every page change reads its switch; the migration adds tables and columns nothing reads until the constant is set. The split is fixed before step 1 and pinned by step 1's record test: checkpoint M for steps 1 to 8, checkpoint N for steps 9 to 11, checkpoint O for step 12. Nothing moves between checkpoints: the newsletter goes out only through Amazon SES (question 2), so the first newsletter needs all eight of M's steps, and if M is late the switch-on day moves.

Part 1 (steps 1 to 8, checkpoint M): what next week needs. Step 1 opens the record, moves both of today's Resend calls behind deliver(), byte for byte, and gathers today's sender addresses into one module, with the switches and constants that govern everything after; step 2 adds migration 0060 (lists marked main mailer or not, contacts keyed by address with the person's stop-all and a spam report's mark kept apart, per-list choices, the do-not-send list, and four columns on the campaign tables), the gate that every send path asks once the engine's rules are on and list mail always asks, the claims and the daily run's order and budget, and pins the suites that hold today's path to it; step 3 builds the signed, non-expiring links, the footer and the RFC 8058 headers, the endpoints a link opens, and keeps list mail off Resend; step 4 builds the newsletter list, the engine's rules (the row decides its path, marked before the send and never sent twice, a throttle ends the run, nothing tried again that may have gone, the link key checked) and batch sizes inside the hosting plan's limits, with the newsletter's four admin methods; step 5 draws the newsletter tab on today's Group email page, holds Groups of members back, and adds the two thin pages a member's link opens, routed always; step 6 lets the media manager send, as the holder of a board seat signed in with a second factor, through WS16's own endpoints only; step 7 adds the Amazon SES sender, signing its own requests in the Worker runtime, the site's own test through it, the rule that it sends only on Workers Paid, and the proof of the sent newsletter, which goes out only through it; step 8 adds the receiver for Amazon's bounces and complaints and closes the checkpoint, with the switch-on change and the cutover change each written out and run green on a throwaway branch. The order puts the shared code first and SES last within M, and the newsletter needs all of it.

Part 2 (steps 9 to 11, checkpoint N): what the first weeks of real sending want and next week does not: the Not delivered list on Group email with an LCA admin's Clear, the record of the cutover as it happened, the media manager's News posts and site banners, which open eleven Admin endpoints and so give them their contracts, and Group email's member groups back, on their own list, LCA tournament email. Its own switch, mailTools, keeps the merge invisible until K turns it on.

Part 3 (step 12, checkpoint O): Resend removed, its own last step after the clean period: the Resend path, its binding, its catch point in the harness, the launch scripts' send halves and its words in the docs, with the seam kept for a later second service (decision 7). K deletes Resend's key and records a week after the merge.

What reaches production with every switch off, by checkpoint: M adds migration 0060 (four empty tables, two list rows, four empty columns; migrate-db.yml), redeploys the daily-emails worker with the mail engine in its bundle and every request it makes unchanged (deploy-worker.yml, since functions/utils and domain changed), and adds ten endpoint methods that answer 404 (or, for GET /api/me/media-manager, false) while MAIL_LISTS_ON is unset; Group email, every page and every email are today's, byte for byte, and the two new paths draw today's empty main area. N adds four endpoint methods that answer 404 while MAIL_TOOLS_ON is unset and changes nothing else that anyone meets. O removes code that no longer runs. K runs npm run db:migrate:preview from the branch before looking at checkpoint M's preview (ordering rule 2), and no preview can send mail: the Preview environment holds no mail key, no link key and no topic.

What is switched on next week, in two changes K merges after checkpoint M. The switch-on change turns mailLists and MAIL_LISTS_ON on together, sets WORKERS_PLAN to 'paid' if K has confirmed Workers Paid, and writes into domain/mail/addresses.ts any sender that differs from what K decided (decision 37); K adds the Media manager seat and assigns it. Then the LCA admins with a second factor, the president and the media manager with a second factor may write and test the newsletter from Group email; the receiver is live; and K proves it and the stored key from the site in Amazon's sandbox. The cutover change sets MAIL_SENDER to 'ses' with WORKERS_PLAN 'paid', once Amazon has approved real sending, K's checks have passed and the account is on Workers Paid; then the first newsletter goes. A member receives it once per address, with a footer saying why, a link to unsubscribe from the newsletter and a link to their email preferences, and the two one-click headers; one press unsubscribes without a sign-in; event and account mail is unchanged and never stopped by an opt-out, and no mail goes to an address that bounced, to a walk-in placeholder or, for list mail, to a reserved example domain.
